residency.test: Resident if you have a domicile in Japan or have had a residence for one year or more.
residency.non_permanent_resident: A resident without Japanese nationality who has had a domicile or residence in Japan for five years or less within the last ten years. Foreign-source income is taxed only if paid in or remitted to Japan.
residency.permanent_resident_for_tax: After five years in ten, worldwide income becomes fully taxable. This five-year cliff is the single most important date for foreign residents in Japan.
residency.worldwide_income: Yes once you become a permanent resident for tax purposes.

headline.inhabitant_tax: a flat 10% local tax, billed in June for the previous calendar year
headline.social_insurance: roughly 15% employee, matched by the employer

standard_deduction.name: Employment income deduction (kyuyo shotoku kojo)
standard_deduction.note: approximation of the statutory tiered formula, which is capped at 1,950,000 above 8,500,000 of salary

personal_allowance.name: Basic deduction (kiso kojo)
personal_allowance.note: raised by the 2025 reform; withdrawn above 24,000,000 of income

local_tax.name: Inhabitant tax (juminzei)
local_tax.note: 6% municipal plus 4% prefectural, with a small per capita levy of about 5,000 on top

surcharges.name: Special reconstruction income tax
surcharges.note: 2.1% of the national income tax, in force through 2037

employee.name: Health insurance
employee.note: Tokyo rate; varies slightly by prefecture

self_employed.name: National health insurance
self_employed.note: municipality-specific formula with a household cap

capital_gains.listed_securities: 20.315% (15% national, 0.315% reconstruction, 5% local), usually withheld in a tokutei kouza account
capital_gains.real_estate: 39.63% if held five years or less, 20.315% if held longer
capital_gains.principal_residence: a 30,000,000 special deduction applies on the sale of your own home
capital_gains.nisa: the NISA account gives a permanent exemption on investment income within generous annual limits and is the default choice for retail investors

quirks: Inhabitant tax is billed a year in arrears. Your first year in Japan feels cheap and your first year after leaving can produce a bill for income you earned while resident - appointing a tax agent before departure avoids problems.

Most employees never file. The employer's year-end adjustment (nenmatsu chosei) in December settles the liability, and a return is needed only for income over 20,000,000, second jobs, or specific deductions like large medical expenses.
The five-year non-permanent resident window is decisive. Foreign income and foreign capital gains are largely outside the net until you cross it, so the timing of asset sales matters enormously.
Furusato nozei lets you redirect part of your inhabitant tax to a municipality of your choice in exchange for local goods, at a net cost of 2,000 yen. It is effectively free money and is widely used.
An exit tax applies to residents holding 100,000,000 yen or more of financial assets who have lived in Japan more than five of the last ten years.

reporting.authority: National Tax Agency (NTA), plus municipal offices for inhabitant tax
reporting.portal: https://www.e-tax.nta.go.jp - e-Tax, and the NTA return preparation corner
reporting.who_must_file: Employees with a single employer and salary up to 20,000,000 are settled by the year-end adjustment. A final return (kakutei shinkoku) is required above that, or with side income over 200,000, multiple employers, or to claim medical, donation or first-year housing loan deductions.

deadlines.what: Final income tax return (kakutei shinkoku) for 2025
Payment of income tax, or the first instalment
Inhabitant tax bills issued for 2025 income; paid in four instalments or through payroll
Consumption tax return for taxable businesses

forms.name: Withholding tax statement from the employer - the key document
Year-end adjustment declarations for dependants and insurance
Separate taxation schedule for capital gains
Required where foreign assets exceed 50,000,000 yen

documents_to_collect: My Number (individual number) card and e-Tax credentials
Gensen choshu hyo from each employer
Insurance premium certificates (life, earthquake, private pension) sent each autumn
Medical expense receipts - a deduction applies above 100,000 yen a year for the household
Furusato nozei donation receipts, or the one-stop exception forms
Housing loan balance certificate for the housing loan tax credit

penalties.late_filing: additional tax of 15% to 20% of the amount due, reduced to 5% for voluntary late filing
penalties.understatement: 10% to 15% additional tax; 35% to 40% where there is concealment
penalties.late_payment: delinquent tax at around 2.4% to 8.7% a year depending on the delay

warnings: The employment income deduction is a close approximation of a tiered statutory formula, not an exact reproduction.
Inhabitant tax uses its own slightly smaller deductions, so the 10% here is applied to the national taxable income base.
Dependant, spouse and insurance deductions are not modelled and reduce the real bill for most households.
